findings.reason: The protected solution is clear, compact, and interview-ready. The children adjacency map reverses the input relation explicitly, and the names process, parent, killed, and stack make the traversal's state and intent immediately legible.

Every paired pid/ppid entry contributes exactly one parent-to-child edge. Starting with kill includes the requested process, and extending the stack with every reached process's direct children inductively visits all descendants. Because traversal follows only those edges from kill in a rooted tree with unique process identifiers, no unrelated process or duplicate can enter the result.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 582 and its Python killProcess(pid, ppid, kill) interface. The app-local solve function preserves the three arguments and returns the killed identifiers in an allowed traversal-dependent order.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065432357 have identical imports, adjacency construction, stack initialization, loop operations, child extension, and return data flow. Their only structural difference is the required Solution.killProcess wrapper.

The three authored deep-chain workloads span 64 through 512 processes and force both complete adjacency construction and complete subtree traversal. The exact protected source passed all eight correctness cases and all three benchmark outputs and performance tiers. A correct control that rescanned every pid/ppid pair for each reached process passed every correctness and benchmark output but failed only scaling with relative growth exponent +1.16 and a 130.82x largest runtime ratio, distinguishing linear preprocessing from quadratic repeated search.

The Approach precisely matches the current source's reverse parent relation, explicit depth-first stack, unrestricted result order, and complete subtree proof. Its O(n) time and O(n) space bounds correctly include adjacency, traversal state, and the required output.

The modular Reference is bound to the authenticated Premium statement's rendered-content hash. It preserves the rooted-tree model, parent-zero convention, cascading kill rule, any-order allowance, both examples and explanation status, all eight constraints, and the source tree image through an independently authored accessible Mermaid diagram.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples now appear first in source order with exact pid, ppid, kill, output membership, and explanation status facts.
The invented root-kill sample was relabelled as a trial, the source singleton was promoted to sample 2, and the formerly hidden nonconsecutive-id and middle-of-chain checks are now visible trials.
Contract boundaries cover n = 1 and n = 50,000, process and parent identifiers 0 and 50,000, unique process ids, equal-length parallel arrays, the sole parent-zero root, and kill guaranteed in pid.

Material semantics cover killing a leaf, an internal process, and the root; preserving unrelated sibling subtrees; multiple children; indirect descendants; a deep chain; nonconsecutive identifiers; and unrestricted output order through unordered-list validators.

An independent parent-walk oracle verified all eight correctness cases and all three benchmark outputs; 46,233 exhaustive rooted-tree/kill pairs and 500 deterministic randomized relabelled trees also agreed with both protected solution forms.
All eight ordinary correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 64-, 256-, and 512-process deep-chain workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
